mu_name_from: MuMain loads group 13 number 12 as Data/Item/Necklace01.bmd: `AccessModel(MODEL_HELPER + i + 12, L"Data\\Item\\", L"Necklace", i + 1)` (ZzzOpenData.cpp:716). OpenMU's 0.75 Jewelery.cs names it 'Pendant of Lightning' (spelt 'Lighting' there and in MuMain's enum). docs/jewellery.md.
why_this_one: The four 0.75 rings and pendants, so they drop as they did (the user, 2026-10-01: 'we need to drop also rings and pendants how it was in MuMain').
profile_note: As Gem05: a small painted sheet on a made object seen close.

stats.note: The item's own row, from OpenMU's 0.75 initialiser, checked against WebZen's item.txt (group 13 row 12: level 21, durability 50, lightning resistance 1).
stats.resistance_note: 1 a plus in this element, the largest of the worn pieces counting (sim/items.h, jewellery).

sheet_from: Data/Item/ring.OZJ (16x16), from MuMain; the .bmd names ring.jpg and all four pieces share it, each on its own cells.
sheet_materials_from: ring.OZJ is silver set with two painted stones: a green one in the top-left cell and a violet one under it, and a silver ramp down the right half. The metal stays the weapon profile's steel; an island wholly on a stone's cell is glass, as Gem05's painted ball (judged from the sheet's pixels).
